steps: This flow compares kinds of tools. First, Claude asks to read a file. That is a built-in tool shipping with the runtime, alongside shell and web, and it goes through hooks and then permissions.
Next, Claude calls your own custom tool for a business system. Notice it passes through exactly the same hook and permission gate. There is one gate for every tool.
Your custom tool runs in-process through an S D K M C P server, so the result comes straight back with no new process, and your business logic stays private.
Now a shared, third-party capability comes from an external M C P server instead, so the call crosses a process boundary to reach it.
The external result comes back the same way. It is the same tool use protocol both ways. Only the process boundary and how widely it can be reused differ.
Next, when Claude needs two independent read-only calls, it can run them in parallel, and that cuts latency.
Finally, when step B needs the result of step A, Claude waits for A, then runs B. Dependent calls run sequentially, independent ones in parallel.
